title: Nought point one plus nought point two

prereqs.why: Every line is a consequence of a double storing a binary fraction rather than a decimal one.

statement:
**What does this print?** Three lines.

The first line is the famous one. The second and third lines together explain why it took you until now to notice.
hints: 0.1 and 0.2 cannot be represented exactly in binary, any more than one third can be written exactly in decimal. So what is `sum` really?
`std::cout` prints a double with six significant digits by default. `precision(17)` asks for enough digits to show every double exactly.
The comparison on the first line is between two values that are both approximations — and they are not the *same* approximation.
